subject: Post-call: dedicated GPU & isolation needs for Nextera ML
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@nextera-ml.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nextera-ml.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: dedicated GPU & isolation needs for Nextera ML

Priya / Tom — thanks again for blocking time this morning. Quick recap from our call plus proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. TL;DR: Nextera is prioritizing predictable throughput for model scoring (1000 qps peak), strict tenant isolation for PHI-derived models, and a rollout during Q3 with a target 99.9% availability SLA.

What we heard (pain points):
- Bursty inference during training-to-serving handoffs causes large latency spikes; current infra autoscaling is too slow.
- Regulatory requirement: model outputs and logs must be isolated per customer/tenant and retained for 90 days with audit trails.
- Cost sensitivity on steady-state token cost; they want a path to reduce unit cost via batching + cache without impacting 95th pct latency.

Goals you stated:
- Reserved GPU pool for production model serving (isolation via dedicated pool or strict tenancy)
- Ops playbook for scale-to-zero avoidance during short bursts and deterministic failover to a lower-cost model variant
- Clear SLA for latency and availability to support sales contracts in Q3

Proposed Redwood approach (summary):
1) Dedicated pool (reserved NVIDIA A100-equivalent capacity) sized for 800 sustained qps with 30% burst headroom to hit 1000 qps peak.
2) Tenant isolation via siloed capacity + per-tenant VPC peering for network controls.
3) Smart routing: primary high-performance model with automatic fallback to a quantized variant if tail latency or capacity thresholds are hit.
4) Ops + runbook: canary rollout, throttling/burst policy, and daily KV prefix cache warmups to reduce cold-starts.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- Sean: share capacity estimate workbook and a 1-page dedicated-capacity summary (attached) — by EOD 5/29.
- Nextera (Priya): confirm retention window and whether audit logs need to be exported to customer-managed S3 — by 6/2.
- Marissa: schedule a technical deep-dive on capacity sizing with Nextera infra & ML infra (30–45m) — propose slots for next week.
- Ben: produce preliminary commercial outline for a 12-month reserved commitment with burst credits — by 6/3.

Attachments: I’ve attached a capacity estimate (nextera_capacity_estimate.xlsx) and a short Redwood dedicated summary (redwood_dedicated_summary.pdf).

If any of the recap items above are off, please flag and I’ll correct. Otherwise I’ll set up the sizing call once I get a confirmation on the retention/audit ask.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
--

Date: 2027-05-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: dedicated GPU & isolation needs for Nextera ML

Thanks Sean — that matches our notes and is a helpful summary. Two clarifications from our side:

1) Retention / audit: we need logs and model invocation metadata retained for 90 days in our own S3 bucket (customer-managed). We also need a signed SOC2 + SOC2 supplemental evidence for the storage/access controls by contract signature.

2) Isolation requirement: for PHI-derived models we prefer physical isolation (dedicated pool) rather than multi-tenant logical isolation. For other lower-sensitivity models, multi-tenant with strict namespacing is fine.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll confirm the list of PHI models and narrow the initial scope (expect to send by 6/2).
- Tom will join the sizing call and provide current traffic percentile numbers and typical batch sizes.

One ask: can Redwood’s runbook include an artifact that shows expected per-token cost delta between the primary model and the quantized fallback at two sequence lengths (128, 512)? That will help our finance team.

Appreciate the quick turn.
Priya
Priya Rao | Head of ML Ops
Nextera ML
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: dedicated GPU & isolation needs for Nextera ML

Folks — forwarding Sean’s recap (below). I pulled the capacity workbook and sketched two sizing options:

Option A (Conservative / isolated): 8 x A100-equivalent reserved nodes, configured as a siloed pool. Expected steady-state cost higher but meets strict PHI isolation. Handles 900 sustained qps with 25% burst headroom.

Option B (Hybrid): 6 x A100-equivalent nodes + auto-burst (on-demand) for peaks. Lower monthly commitment, more complex failover; requires ~6–8 hour autoscaler warmup to consistently hit peak.

Technical notes / questions for Nextera before the sizing call:
- What is your 95th and 99th percentile latency SLO for scoring? (Priya — you mentioned <200ms at 95th earlier; please confirm.)
- Do you require model weights to be encrypted with a customer-managed KMS?
- Any preference on quantization formats (e.g., int8) for fallback? We can run a quick eval on model artifacts if they can share them via a secure transfer link.

I’ll propose 3 slots for a 45-min technical deep dive tomorrow/Friday. Sean — can you add the HubSpot deal link and the capacity workbook to the invite?

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
